statement: For any finite Dirichlet polynomial F_0(t) = sum_{n<=N} c_n e^{-it log n} with c_n = Lambda(n) n^{-1/2-a} and smooth window W in S(R) or C_c^infty(R), the real grade jet cross-term X_{N,W} = Re <F_0, ddot F_0>_W decomposes into diagonal and off-diagonal sums: X_{N,W} = (log tau)^2 Re sum_{m,n<=N} c_m bar(c_n) I_{m,n}(W), where I_{m,n}(W) = (-a L_n + a^2 L_n^2) hat{W}(xi_{mn}) + i (L_n - 2a L_n^2) hat{tW}(xi_{mn}) - L_n^2 hat{t^2 W}(xi_{mn}), with L_n = log n and xi_{mn} = log(m/n). Finite windows do not force off-diagonal terms to vanish; off-diagonal terms are structurally present and certified non-zero for concrete witness (N=3, a=1.5, sigma_W=1.0: X_diag approx -0.0515509, X_full approx -0.0240200, X_offdiag approx +0.0275309).

quantified_variables.name: W
quantified_variables.domain: W in S(R) or C_c^infty(R), W >= 0, int W = 1

hypotheses: F_0(t) = sum_{n<=N} c_n e^{-it log n}
ddot F_0(t) = (log tau)^2 sum_{n<=N} c_n [ -(a+it) log n + (a+it)^2 (log n)^2 ] e^{-it log n}
object_studied: Finite-window Dirichlet polynomial grade second-variation real cross-term X_{N,W}
fourier_normalization: Centered coordinates z = s - 1/2 = a + it; tau = 2pi; Fourier transform hat{f}(xi) = int_{-infty}^infty f(t) e^{-it xi} dt
measure_and_window: Admissible smooth test window W(t) dt
order_of_limits: Finite sum N < infinity; 1D integration over real line
exact_conclusion: X_{N,W} = (log tau)^2 Re sum_{m,n<=N} c_m bar(c_n) I_{m,n}(W); matches 1D numerical quadrature within certified tolerance; off-diagonal terms are structurally present and certified non-zero for concrete parameters
logical_negation: X_{N,W} = (Diagonal sum) for all admissible finite windows W (FALSIFIED: finite windows do not force off-diagonal terms to vanish)
falsification_attempts: Evaluated 2-term and 4-term Dirichlet polynomials under Schwartz Gaussian and C_c^infty bump windows
Verified certified discrepancy |Full - Diag| > 0 in Arb for N=3, a=1.5, sigma_W=1.0
Tested that off-diagonal terms vanish only in the infinite Cesaro limit T -> infinity, which is decoupled from finite window variance

external_sources.source: Montgomery & Vaughan (1974), Hilbert's inequality, J. London Math. Soc. (2) 8, 73-82
external_sources.theorem: Theorem 2 (Mean value bound for Dirichlet polynomials)

external_sources.theorem: Chapter I, Section 5 (Parseval equality for B^2 space)

remaining_analytic_dependencies: Infinite series extension to completed xi-function (OBL-DERIVE-FULL-WINDOWED-ZETA-CROSS-TERM)
